posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

Death isn't a single switch that shuts down your entire body at once. When your heart stops beating and your brain goes silent, trillions of cells inside you are still alive, desperately trying to keep themselves running. Death isn't a single moment, but a slow and surprisingly complex process that can last for weeks.

What actually happens when you die? What makes death so mysterious, and which cells are the last survivors within your body? Watch our full video to find out!

Some places make you want to take the scenic route and stay a little longer. 🌿💦 ⁠
Malingarna in Dalarna, Sweden, is one of them, the perfect spot for a beautiful drive, a lakeside picnic or a refreshing swim surrounded by nature.⁠
🎥: @sophiabergholm

Shopping in Seoul comes with a little challenge! 😂🪨 ⁠
At this store, even getting through the entrance is an adventure. ⁠
⁠
There's a giant rock blocking the way, and figuring out how to get past it is entirely up to you. Would you make it inside?⁠
🎥: @leeyihan0706⁠

There’s a little LOVE hidden in the heart of Europe, and it’s called sLOVEnia 💚

In the country with love in its name, opposites attract. Here, the Alps meet the Adriatic Sea and the mysterious Karst, while sunlit hills roll toward the Pannonian Plain. Everything is close and connected, so in one trip you can wake up by an alpine lake, wander through an island town, and end the day watching the sunset over the sea.

Slovenia is full of surprises! There are ancient forests where brown bears roam

In The Farm Family Project, photographer @rob.macinnis brought the style of classic family portraits to the barnyard. Between 2007 and 2022, he photographed cows, pigs, sheep, goats, and chickens, then digitally combined the shots into carefully arranged group portraits. ⁠
⁠
The result looks like a holiday card, with each animal getting the kind of attention usually saved for people.⁠
⁠
Which one would be the “cool uncle” of this family? 😂

In the middle of China’s Taklamakan Desert, fall arrives in a way few people would expect. ⁠
⁠
These hardy trees grow along rivers and water sources in one of the driest places on Earth, and some can live for centuries. ⁠
⁠
Locals have a saying that they live for a thousand years, stand for a thousand years after they die, and take another thousand years to decay.⁠
⁠
By: @kevinnyunphoto

Is this the biggest mango tree in the world? 🥭🌳 ⁠
⁠
With a canopy this enormous, it almost looks like an entire forest growing from a single tree! Nature really knows how to show off. 🤯⁠
🎥: @shelleyplants

High in the Himalayan foothills of central Nepal, Gurung honey hunters have been taking on one of the world’s most daring harvests for generations. ⁠
⁠
Clinging to handmade rope ladders as high as 200 feet up sheer cliffs, they use smoke to calm the bees, then cut away the honeycomb with long bamboo poles and lower it down in baskets.⁠
⁠
Photographer @andrewnewey spent time with the Gurung people 13 years ago to document this ancient tradition. ⁠
⁠

@antronoid captured London’s Tower Bridge at 7 a.m. as thick fog rolled over the city.⁠
⁠
Lights from passing traffic streaked across the bridge, and just at the right moment, flocks of birds flew straight through the frame. ⁠
⁠
This is a real photo, not AI! Just perfect timing and a lucky morning. 📸

A journey of faith, one step at a time. 🙏⛰️ At Tirumala in India, many devotees choose to climb around 3,550 steps to reach the sacred Tirupati Balaji Temple. ⁠
⁠
For them, every step is an act of devotion, making the climb just as meaningful as reaching the destination. ❤️⁠
🎥: @_swatiiiiii_13

With its dark skin speckled in blue and patches of bright orange, it’s easy to see how the galaxy frog got its name. These tiny frogs grow to only about an inch long and live in the wet forests of India’s southern Western Ghats, where they tend to hide under rotting logs.⁠
⁠
Photographer @hadlee_renjith captured these close-ups in Munnar, Kerala. The galaxy frog is listed as Vulnerable, as it lives in a small range and is very sensitive to heat, drying out and disturbance.⁠

A room built from the remains of the dead, and still standing more than 800 years later. 💀⁠
Hidden beside the Basilica of Santo Stefano in Milan, the San Bernardino alle Ossa ossuary was built in 1210 to house bones displaced from the cemetery of the nearby Brolo Hospital. ⁠

They typically roam the world’s oceans, but one group off the coast of New Zealand seems to have settled in the South Taranaki Bight. Unfortunately, this snake’s habitat is used frequently for agricultural purposes—growing coffee plants and ornamental ferns—which has decreased suitable habitat. Indris are the largest lemur species in the world, and they are known for their astonishingly loud, musical singing. Found in Madagascar, indris are among the many animals unique to the island—but their habitat is threatened. Now, to estimate the population, scientists are using a process known as passive acoustic monitoring to map the density and abundance of the endemic species.
